title: Brown and Wild Rice, Cooked, No Salt

content.title: About
content.content: Brown and wild rice is a blend of whole‑grain brown rice and wild rice grains, cooked by steaming or boiling without added salt. It has a nutty aroma, slightly chewy texture, and a high dietary fiber content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wild rice is not a true rice; it belongs to the water‑grass family.
The blend is popular in low‑glycemic diets because it raises blood sugar more slowly than white rice.
Cooking retains more B‑vitamins and minerals than polishing white rice.
Wild rice contains more protein than most common rice varieties.
Combining the two grains enhances flavor complexity and texture.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: The blend provides about 5 g of protein per 100 g, beneficial for vegetarians.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps stabilize blood glucose levels, useful for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Contains magnesium and phosphorus
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nerve signaling, and bone health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients such as phenolic acids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to rice.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Wild rice can accumulate arsenic from soil; varied diet is recommended.

items.title: High phytic acid
items.content: Phytic acid may reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked brown and wild rice works as a side dish, a base for salads, soups, and Buddha bowls. Add it to vegetable stews, use in casseroles, or serve with yogurt‑based sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
